verdict.headline: EV9-IR-01 is repaired and the repair is independently confirmed. My own enumeration of the hostile space, written from the rule prose alone, reproduces the published census EXACTLY - 2778 paths, 590 container, 2188 scalar leaf, 359 dict, 15 values, 42029 enumerated, 75 no-op, 41954 executed - and my own wider fuzz found zero escapes where v9 had 44. Every published quantity in hostileInputTotalityContract is true of these bytes. The repair is load-bearing: with the guard removed I measured 874 unguarded escapes. I did find that both AST self-scans are SYNTACTIC rather than semantic - a path consumer reached through an alias, getattr, a dispatch table or a renamed copy is invisible to PR-23, and a second selftest entrypoint tested through a set method and dispatched through an alias is invisible to PR-21 - and I demonstrated each with a full green run. Neither can produce a false accept on these bytes, because these bytes contain no indirection at all; both are forward-looking, and I grade them non-blocking under the standard this corpus applied to the analogous D40 overstatement in the d9-exit-contract.v1.14 review, which PASSED with an ADVISORY.
verdict.verdictRationale: The v9 REJECT turned on a rule that was FALSE of the frozen bytes: requiredEscapes was published as 0 and 44 were measurable. Nothing of that kind survives here. I re-derived every published number independently and all match; I drove 76515 hostile cases of my own construction through the unguarded layers (22224 with a value alphabet the author does not use, 12337 combinatorial two-position, plus the author's 41954 which I re-ran) and measured zero unguarded escapes, zero guarded escapes and zero silent cases. The rule pathConsumerGuard states is TRUE of these bytes and I verified it exhaustively at the AST level: every reference to _path_steps, _resolve and _assign anywhere in the source is a direct call, there is not one alias, bare reference, attribute call or getattr, and exactly one of the fifteen consumption sites is candidate-supplied. My two findings are that the artifact describes its enforcement instruments as closed over a semantic property when they are closed over a syntactic one, and that one closure sentence is literally false about its own source. Both are the D9-v1.14 shape: the RULE is accurate and completely enforced, the OVERSTATEMENT is in a subordinate clause describing the instrument, and neither can produce a false accept on these bytes. Grading them blocking would be inconsistent with the standard this corpus applied three artifacts ago.

independentEnumeration.question: Is 2778 actually complete - unlimited depth, every array index, leaves AND containers?
independentEnumeration.answer: YES. My enumeration matches 2778 exactly and I found no path it misses.
independentEnumeration.method: I wrote a recursive walker directly from the rule sentence in hostileInputTotalityContract.rule, without reading _enumerate_positions, emitting one position for the root plus one for every dict value and every list item at unlimited depth. I then compared my totals to the published census and independently audited the two ways an enumeration of this shape can silently lose ground: path-string collisions and unaddressable keys.
independentEnumeration.whyPathsNotRoundTrippingIsGenuinelyZero: The round-trip filter can silently drop positions whose path string is not re-parsable by _path_steps, which would let the artifact publish a clean 0 while hiding unreachable regions. I checked this directly rather than trusting the counter: every one of the 2778 path strings is distinct (no collision can mask a position), and every dict key in the whole document matches [A-Za-z0-9_]+ so every key is expressible in the path grammar. A key containing '.', '-' or a space would have produced a positive pathsNotRoundTripping; there are none. The published 0 is real, not an artifact of the filter.
independentEnumeration.coverageOfPathLeaves: I separately enumerated every string leaf whose position is path-shaped. There are 52: 44 at semanticBindingRegistry.entries[*].boundArtifactPaths[*] and 8 at successorDelta.retainedHistoricalLabelPaths[*]. The 44 are genuinely candidate-supplied and genuinely consumed as paths by _registry_findings; the 8 are compared against a checker constant and never resolved. The witness family the narrowing suite requires is therefore the correct and complete one.
independentEnumeration.positionsIWasUnableToFault: None. I looked specifically for positions inside empty containers (successorDelta.grammarEditorialDelta is an empty list in v10, so the v9 defect site has no leaf to inject at in this generation - the surviving candidate-supplied family is the registry one, and the generator reaches all 44 of it), for positions behind non-round-tripping keys, and for positions lost to path-string aliasing. None exist.

independentHostileMeasurement.extendedAlphabetRationale: The published measurement quantifies over POSITIONS but its value alphabet is a fixed 15-element list. Totality at a position is not established by 15 values, so I built eight structured hostile values the author does not use - row lists carrying empty and unparsable path strings, objects with path/paths/producer/obligation/binding keys carrying unparsable strings, path lists, and a deep nested carrier - and drove all eight at all 2778 positions. Zero escapes and zero silent cases. This is a strictly stronger result than the author claims and I record it as an independent strengthening, not as a defect.
independentHostileMeasurement.combinatorialRationale: The artifact's own retainedResiduals[9] states plainly that a single value is injected at a single position per case and that a zero escape count is therefore a bound on single-position non-totality, not a proof of totality. I tested outside that bound: 12337 two-position cases, 9000 uniformly random pairs plus the full ordered pair set within semanticBindingRegistry. Zero unguarded escapes. The residual is honestly stated and I found nothing it conceals.
independentHostileMeasurement.silentCountStrength: I checked whether silent==0 is a real measurement or an artifact of the whole-object successor-equality layer firing on every changed candidate. Over a 3280-case sample I re-ran with with_equality=False: silent is still 0. The zero is therefore carried by the semantic layers and not by whole-object comparison alone.

guardRemovalMakesTheUnguardedLayerRaiseA.method: In a disposable copy I deleted the try/except Malformed around the candidate-supplied _resolve(candidate, str(path)) in _registry_findings and re-ran both the AST scan and the runtime matrix.
guardRemovalMakesTheUnguardedLayerRaiseA.astResult: scannedFunctions 65 unchanged, guardedCallSites 9 -> 8, unguardedCallSites 0 -> 1, reported site '_registry_findings line 2722'
guardRemovalMakesTheUnguardedLayerRaiseA.runtimeResult: the same 41954 cases over the same 2778 paths went from 0 unguarded escapes to 874, guardedEscapes still 0, silent still 0. First escapes are at recursiveRequestIdExclusion with Malformed 'path recursiveRequestIdExclusion.rule: key rule is absent'.
guardRemovalMakesTheUnguardedLayerRaiseA.conclusion: The guard is genuinely load-bearing at the one candidate-supplied consumption site this generation has, and the scan detects its direct removal.

predecessorFindingDispositions.basis: The v9 defect was that _grammar_delta_findings called _path_steps(path)[-1] unguarded on a candidate string, and that _hostile_nodes could not inject at scalar leaves so the 44 escapes were unobservable. Both halves are repaired. (a) The consumption now goes through _steps_or_none, a total accessor returning None, with a deterministic finding on the None branch; I read the site and confirmed it. (b) The enumerator now includes scalar leaves and my independent enumeration confirms it reaches all 2778 positions. (c) I re-derived the v9 escape family in v10 terms: successorDelta.grammarEditorialDelta is EMPTY in v10, so the v9 site has no leaf to inject at, and the surviving candidate-supplied family is the 44 boundArtifactPaths leaves, which are reached and which produce deterministic findings rather than exceptions - visible live in the dirty-base run as "SB-01-INDETERMINATE-OR-ERROR-DOMINATES: bound path '' is absent or not a parsable path". (d) My own 76515-case fuzz, wider in both value alphabet and arity than the author's, measured zero escapes. requiredEscapes: 0 is TRUE of these bytes.
predecessorFindingDispositions.residualNoted: The closure sentence 'a fourth omitted site cannot recur silently as the third one did' is a durability claim I falsified - see EV10-IR-01. That does not reopen EV9-IR-01, whose rule is satisfied by these bytes.

predecessorFindingDispositions.myDisposition: CLOSED - the repair the v9 reviewer ASKED FOR is implemented exactly as specified; the closure PROSE overshoots it
predecessorFindingDispositions.basis: The v9 reviewer's required repair item 1 was, verbatim, to 'collect every Compare node in main() that tests a string literal beginning --, and require that set to equal the flag set implied by checkerModeContract.entrypoints'. _selftest_entrypoint_scan does precisely that, plus DECLARED_FLAGS, plus a dispatch count and a lexical-guard requirement. I reproduced the v8 defect (a second dispatch under --foundation-selftest tested with `in`) and it is CAUGHT. Three further variants - a runtime-concatenated flag literal, a startswith prefix test, and a set-method flag test with a direct dispatch - are also caught, each by a different clause. Only the combination of a set-method flag test AND an aliased dispatch evades, which is beyond what the v9 repair specified. The finding is closed; the closure sentence is separately inaccurate and is recorded as EV10-IR-02.

In v9, `check-evidence-v9.py <clean> <dirty> --selftest` exited 0 having silently dropped the second path. In v10 I ran ten argument vectors: two positionals, an unknown flag, -x, --emit-candidate combined with --selftest, --emit-candidate with a positional, the empty string, a bare --, a case-variant flag and --selftest=1. All ten exit 2 with a named EV10-UNSUPPORTED-INVOCATION reason. A repeated declared flag is accepted under set semantics, exactly as checkerModeContract.argumentDiscipline declares, and I confirmed `--selftest --selftest` still runs the suite to a green SELFTEST-PASS.

predecessorFindingDispositions.myDisposition: CLOSED - CONFIRMED at the source and scan level
predecessorFindingDispositions.basis: selftest() now prints the candidate path it was given rather than the constant, and _selftest_entrypoint_scan additionally computes bindingLiteralInSelftest, requiring that selftest() contain NO string constant equal to 'evidence.v10.json'. I confirmed the live scan reports bindingLiteralInSelftest false, and I confirmed the source self-mutation 'selftest-label-is-a-literal', which re-inserts the constant, is reported. I then closed it by EXECUTION, which is the only way to be sure: I copied the candidate to artifacts/renamed-candidate.json in a disposable tree and ran `--selftest` against that path. It printed 'SELFTEST-PASS: renamed-candidate.json' and exited 0. The label is the actual path checked, not a source literal.

_warm_context() rebuilds the derivation context from PINNED authority when it is cold, and reads nothing from the candidate, so warming cannot make the comparison self-referential - I checked that specifically, because a warmer that consulted the candidate would convert a fail-closed degradation into a self-fulfilling pass. PR-25-COLD-CONTEXT-FULL-STRENGTH clears both context and census, re-runs the COMPLETE candidate_layers over the derived successor, requires zero findings AND requires the context to have been rebuilt. The double requirement is what makes it non-vacuous.

retainedResiduals[8] states the position accurately: the grammar is bound through its machine-readable tag, field-name and field-order table; the prose is checked for the exact set rule only and the remainder could diverge without detection. That is the same claim the v9 reviewer confirmed, unchanged and not quietly upgraded.

newFindings.finding: PR-23 is published as a structural guarantee: 'This is enforced structurally rather than site by site: the checker parses its own source, computes the function closure reachable from the checking entrypoints, and requires every consumption inside that closure to be lexically enclosed by a handler for Malformed', and the EV9-IR-01 closure adds 'so a fourth omitted site cannot recur silently as the third one did'. The scan recognises a consumption only as an ast.Call whose func is an ast.Name literally spelled _path_steps, _resolve or _assign, and it computes reachability only by following ast.Name calls to module-level ast.FunctionDef nodes. Any consumption that is not that exact syntax is invisible to it, and so is any function it reaches only through such a call.
newFindings.evidence: I built nine indirection variants of the exact EV9-IR-01 victim site and ran each through _path_guard_scan. CAUGHT: a direct unguarded call, a call inside a list comprehension, a call inside an immediately-invoked lambda. EVADED: (V2) a module-level alias `_EV10_ALIAS = _path_steps` then `_EV10_ALIAS(path)`; (V3) a function-local alias `_local = _path_steps` then `_local(path)`; (V4) `getattr(sys.modules[__name__], '_path_steps')(path)`; (V6) a dispatch table `_EV10_TABLE['p'](path)`; (V7) a renamed byte-for-byte copy of the parser under a new name not in PATH_CONSUMER_NAMES. I then built the decisive additive case, because the five evasions above all removed the existing guarded site and would have tripped the absentRequired tripwire: I ADDED a module-level alias (an Assign, not a FunctionDef, so the function closure is unchanged) plus a fourth unguarded candidate-supplied consumption inside _grammar_delta_findings, gated on two simultaneously-hostile positions so the single-position generator can never reach it. The live scan then reported scannedFunctions 65, guardedCallSites 9, unguardedCallSites 0 - the published values, unchanged to the digit - and the full checker printed the complete green banner with 26/26 probes and exit 0. A fourth omitted site did recur silently.
newFindings.whyNotBlocking: It cannot produce a false accept on THESE bytes, and I verified that at the AST level rather than assuming it: I enumerated every ast.Name reference to _path_steps, _resolve, _assign and _steps_or_none anywhere in the frozen source and there are fifteen, all of them direct calls, with not one alias, bare load, attribute call, getattr or comprehension-captured reference. The frozen source contains no indirection for the scan to miss. The nine consumer call sites inside the reachable closure are all guarded, exactly as published, and exactly one of them - _registry_findings line 2723 - is candidate-supplied. The RULE the artifact states is true and completely enforced over these bytes; the overstatement is confined to the subordinate clause describing the instrument's generality and its durability under future edits. This is the same shape the d9-exit-contract.v1.14 independent review graded ADVISORY while returning PASS, and any future edit to this checker produces a different SHA-256 and a new artifact requiring fresh review, which is the control that actually covers the durability class.
newFindings.reproducibleCondition: In a disposable copy of the tree, insert `_EV10_HIDDEN = _path_steps` as a module-level statement anywhere above _steps_or_none, and inside _grammar_delta_findings insert, immediately before `declared_paths.append(path)`, `if row.get('predecessorValue') == 1.5 and row.get('successorValue') == 1.5: _ = _EV10_HIDDEN(row.get('path', ''))`. Run `python3 -I -B artifacts/check-evidence-v10.py`. It exits 0 with the full green banner and unguardedCallSites still 0.
requiredRepair: Make the consumption predicate semantic rather than name-syntactic: treat any ast.Call whose callee cannot be statically resolved to a known-total accessor as a consumption, or at minimum treat any ast.Name that BINDS a path consumer (an alias assignment, a container literal, a default argument, a decorator) as itself a consumption site.
Refuse getattr and attribute-form calls onto this module inside the reachable closure, so the module object cannot be used as an indirection layer.

Derive PATH_CONSUMER_NAMES rather than declaring it: require that no function inside the closure other than the three declared consumers contains a `raise Malformed` on a path parse, so a renamed copy of the parser is reported.

Extend the reachability walk to ast.AsyncFunctionDef, to FunctionDefs nested inside module-level if/try/with blocks, and to ClassDef method bodies, none of which are currently in the `functions` dict.

ALTERNATIVELY, and sufficient on its own: narrow the published prose so it claims only what the scan proves - that every SYNTACTICALLY DIRECT consumption inside the closure is lexically guarded - and drop the durability clause 'a fourth omitted site cannot recur silently as the third one did'.
newFindings.repairSize: either one predicate change in _collect_path_calls plus a binding-site check, or a two-clause prose narrowing in pathConsumerGuard.rule and the EV9-IR-01 closure

newFindings.finding: The published closure for EV9-IR-02 states: 'The reachability scan collects every string literal beginning with two hyphens anywhere in this checker's source and requires that set to equal the declared flag set.' It does not. It collects only literals that appear inside an ast.Compare node, plus the literals of the DECLARED_FLAGS constant. The checker's own comment at line 3327 states the narrower behaviour explicitly and gives a sound rationale for it - inert data such as the refusal battery's hostile vectors gates nothing - so the code is deliberate and the closure sentence simply does not describe it.
newFindings.evidence: One AST pass over the frozen source: string constants beginning '--' ANYWHERE are ['--', '--bogus', '--emit', '--emit-candidate', '--foundation-selftest', '--selftest']; the literals the scan actually collects are ['--emit-candidate', '--selftest']. Four literals are present in the source and not collected. Were the sentence true, the scan's flag set would be six elements, would not equal sorted(DECLARED_FLAGS), and the checker would report a finding on its own clean source. Separately I falsified the sentence's practical consequence: of five second-entrypoint variants, four are caught, but `if flags.issuperset({'--covert'}): _s = selftest; return _s(...)` - a flag tested through a set method so no literal lands in a Compare, and a dispatch through a local alias so dispatchCount stays 1 - evades every clause. Inserted into a disposable copy of main(), the checker prints the full green banner with 26/26 probes and exit 0, re-creating the v8 EV8-IR-06 undocumented-entrypoint defect.
newFindings.whyAdvisoryAndNotHigher: The v9 reviewer's required repair specified Compare nodes verbatim, and that is exactly what was built; the repair asked for is done. checkerModeContract.selftestReachability, which is the artifact's normative statement of the property, says only 'the set of command flag literals in the source must equal declaredFlags' - defensible, since a literal that is never tested against the argument vector is not a command flag. The false sentence is confined to one subordinate clause of one reviewFindingTransfers closure. It cannot produce a false accept on these bytes: I independently enumerated the flag-shaped literals and the two real ones are exactly the two declared, there is exactly one selftest dispatch and it is lexically guarded by --selftest. Under the corpus's own D9-v1.14 precedent - an overstated justificatory clause about a neighbouring region, graded ADVISORY with a PASS verdict - this is ADVISORY.
newFindings.reproducibleCondition: Run one AST pass collecting every ast.Constant str starting '--' and compare with the same collection restricted to descendants of ast.Compare nodes; the difference is ['--', '--bogus', '--emit', '--foundation-selftest']. For the entrypoint evasion, insert the two-line covert dispatch above into main() in a disposable tree and run the checker in normal mode; it exits 0.

observations.note: I was asked to verify a claim that the predecessor's silent count of 0 was an artifact of not resetting the probe log between cases rather than a measurement. TWO results. First, the FROZEN CANDIDATE MAKES NO SUCH CLAIM: I searched evidence.v10.json for every occurrence of 'silent', 'probe log', 'contamina', 'reset' and 'per-case' and there is no assertion about v9's number anywhere in it. The only text is a docstring inside check-evidence-v10.py at lines 3619-3621 describing v10's OWN hygiene: 'The probe log is restored to its entry state before every case, so the silent-case count is a genuine per-case measurement and not an artifact of state left behind by an earlier case.' That is a statement about v10 and it is true of v10. Second, I tested the underlying proposition anyway, because it matters whether a published number survived a full independent review while being wrong. I re-executed the v9 matrix loop against the v9 layers twice, once as shipped and once with the v10 per-case reset applied: 2992 cases both ways, 0 escapes both ways, SILENT 0 BOTH WAYS. The contamination is real as a mechanism - v9 line 2451 reads authority.probe_log inside a checking layer, so a probe driven False by one case does persist - but on this corpus it changes no measured value. The correct statement is that v9's silent count was measured on an instrument that COULD have been contaminated, and was not. v10's reset is genuine hygiene that removes a latent hazard; it does not correct an error. I record this because the narrative I was handed - that a published v9 number was wrong - is not supported by measurement, and, to the artifact's credit, is not asserted by the artifact.

I was told PR-23 found a fourth unguarded consumer in build_grammar. The frozen candidate does not say that, and the distinction matters. build_grammar's _resolve and _assign at lines 1894 and 1899 consume paths from the GRAMMAR_DELTA checker constant against the PINNED predecessor grammar; neither the path nor the object is candidate-supplied. Guarding it is correct defensive hardening but it is not a second EV9-IR-01. Of the nine guarded call sites in the reachable closure - _producer_obligation_findings 2798, _registry_findings 2723, _round_trips 3531, _steps_or_none 1784, build_grammar 1894 and 1899, hostile_matrix 3641, 3662 and 3670 - exactly ONE, _registry_findings 2723, consumes a candidate-supplied string. The scan over-approximates, which is the right direction, and the artifact's published count of 9 is a count of consumer call sites in the closure and is accurate as such. The artifact nowhere claims all nine are candidate-supplied.

pathConsumerGuard.rule requires consumption 'inside a handler for Malformed that emits a deterministic finding'. The scan verifies only the first half: _handles_malformed accepts a bare `except:`, `except Exception` and `except BaseException` as well as `except Malformed`, and nothing checks that the handler body produces a finding. A site guarded by `except Malformed: pass` would count toward guardedCallSites and would silently skip its check. On these bytes every handler does emit a finding - I read all nine - and the runtime silent-case counter is an independent backstop, so this is not exploitable here. It is the natural place the property will erode next.

_own_tree reads HERE/CHECKER from disk rather than analysing the bytes the interpreter is executing, so the three self-scans have a genuine time-of-check gap against the checker's own source. I tested it: I launched the checker from a source containing an unguarded consumer and swapped a clean copy onto disk three seconds later. No false green resulted - exit 1 with 15 findings, because the runtime totality layer reports the defect independently of the scan. Defence in depth held. The gap is nonetheless real, and it is worth stating that the scans' subject is the file, not the process. This is bounded by the fact that the checker cannot self-pin at all, so any change to it yields a new artifact requiring fresh review.

successorDelta.grammarEditorialDelta is an empty list, so the loop body of _grammar_delta_findings - the exact site of EV9-IR-01 - never executes on the frozen candidate. The site is still exercised by the hostile matrix, because the nested-object injection [{'unknown': 1}] at that position installs a row, and it is exercised by the mutation suite. The repair at that site is therefore genuine but its live load-bearing weight in v10 rests on the registry consumption, which is why I ran the guard-removal proof against _registry_findings rather than the historic site. It also means the v9 escape family of 44 at grammarEditorialDelta[N].path has no analogue in v10, and the 44 the narrowing suite witnesses is a different, coincidentally equal-sized family at boundArtifactPaths.

_path_guard_scan builds its function table from `subject.body` filtered to ast.FunctionDef. It therefore never sees an ast.AsyncFunctionDef at module level, a FunctionDef nested inside a module-level if/try/with block, or any method of the twelve ClassDefs in this source. None exist today in a path-consuming role - I checked all twelve classes - so nothing is missed on these bytes. It is the same syntactic-closure weakness as EV10-IR-01 and repairs with it.

The generator-narrowing battery is a genuinely good instrument. It does not merely check that the numbers changed; it requires the narrowed space to be strictly smaller in both paths and cases, requires scalarLeafPaths to become zero, requires the widened space to reach a named witness family, and requires the narrowed space NOT to reach it.
